title: Distributionally robust decision-making under ambiguity: case study of water environmental management
summary: Decision-making under uncertainty is ubiquitous in environmental project planning. Environmental processes such as a streamflow discharge often present a subexponential memory, where the autocorrelation persists for a long time. In addition, optimization problems driven by environmental processes encounter the issue of model ambiguity because of a lack of sufficient data for model identification.
